title: Trump, Xi and Putin Plan Unprecedented Joint Meeting at APEC, Officials Say
excerpt: The White House confirmed plans for a trilateral on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen, AP reported, while CNN noted Beijing and Moscow have yet to officially confirm participation. U.S. officials say no agreement is expected.
body:
• Officials say the leaders of the United States, China and Russia plan to meet on Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, according to the Associated Press — a plan the White House confirmed on Friday, the AP reported.
  • Beijing and Moscow have yet to officially confirm participation in the trilateral summit, CNN reported, so the meeting should be read as planned, not as agreed by all three sides on the public record.
  • APEC's leaders' meeting is set for November 18 and 19 in Shenzhen, Reuters reported; Bloomberg, cited in other reporting, put the planned trilateral on November 19.
  • A senior U.S. official told reporters no agreements are expected: the talks are described as an entry point on nuclear arms, with Iran also planned for discussion and Ukraine, the official said, not planned.

The leaders of the United States, China and Russia plan to meet on Thursday on the sidelines of next week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China's tech hub of Shenzhen, the Associated Press reported, in what would be an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world's biggest nuclear powers. Plans for the three-way meeting with Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin were confirmed on Friday by the White House, according to the AP.

That confirmation is American. CNN, reporting the same White House announcement on Friday, added a material caveat: “Beijing and Moscow have yet to officially confirm participation in the trilateral summit.” Readers should hold the story in those terms — a meeting Washington says is planned, whose other two participants have not, in the reporting read for this article, publicly confirmed their attendance in that format.

What officials say the talks would cover

The meeting will focus on nuclear non-proliferation, CNN reported, a topic Trump has said he believes could yield a new agreement between the world's biggest nuclear-armed states. White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters, according to CNN: “The President has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world.”

U.S. officials downplayed the prospect of a deal. “We do not expect to get to any kind of agreement,” a senior U.S. official said, according to both CNN and the AP. “I would characterize this as the entry point, the first conversation, certainly at the leader level, between these countries.”

“We do not expect to get to any kind of agreement. I would characterize this as the entry point, the first conversation, certainly at the leader level, between these countries.”

— Senior U.S. official, as reported by AP and CNN

Trump does plan to discuss the Iran war with Xi and Putin, but will steer away from discussing Ukraine, a U.S. official said, according to the AP. Officials also said the leaders planned to discuss Iran, CNN reported.

Why a nuclear conversation, and why now

The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States expired in February, removing caps on the two largest atomic arsenals for the first time in more than half a century, the AP reported. When that treaty — New START — expired, Trump rejected a Russian call to extend the two-country deal for another year and called for a new deal that includes China, according to the AP.

The arsenals are unequal. Beijing's arsenal of more than 600 warheads, according to Pentagon estimates cited by the AP, is far smaller than the inventories held by the United States and Russia, each estimated to have more than 5,000 warheads. With its stockpile dwarfed by the other two, China has shown little interest in developing a nuclear pact, the AP reported.

The APEC setting

The APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting is set for November 18 and 19, preceded by a CEO summit on November 17-18, Reuters reported in an explainer carried by BusinessWorld. China has said Xi will chair the leaders' meeting and deliver remarks, and Trump, Putin and Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. are among those expected, Reuters said. APEC groups 21 member economies and, Reuters noted, does not include India.

Analysts quoted by the AP said expectations are low that the talks will lead to major breakthroughs, and that they will be heavier in symbolism than substance. The AP also reported that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concern that the trilateral could serve as a platform for discussing a possible Ukraine deal behind Kyiv's back — even though a U.S. official said Ukraine is not planned for discussion.

What to watch

Two things will settle whether this becomes the meeting Washington describes: a public confirmation from Beijing and from Moscow, and what, if anything, the three leaders say jointly afterwards. Until then, the accurate description is the one in the officials' own words — a planned, unprecedented joint meeting on the sidelines of APEC, presented by U.S. officials as the start of a nuclear conversation, not the announcement of an agreement.
image_caption: Officials attend an APEC China 2026 senior officials meeting in Dalian. The APEC leaders meeting is set for November 18 and 19 in Shenzhen, where officials say a Trump-Xi-Putin meeting is planned.
nri_angle: A planned first-ever U.S.-China-Russia leaders' meeting at APEC in Shenzhen would reshape the geopolitics diaspora readers follow on trade, energy and security, though Beijing and Moscow have not yet confirmed it publicly.
